## 离散时间系统函数

Recall the response of a DT LTI system to the input $x[n]$ is

$$
y[n]=(x * h)[n]
$$

where $h$ is the impulse response of the system.
If $x$ and $h$ have $z$-transforms, the convolution property implies

$$
Y(z)=X(z) H(z)
$$

in their common ROC.
If the ROC has a nonempty interior point, the system function (aka transfer function) $H(z)$ uniquely determines $h$ and hence system properties through the Laurent series expansion

$$
H(z)=\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty} h[n] z^{-n}
$$

## 因果性

Recall $h$ is right-sided iff its ROC is the exterior of a circle, i.e. $R_{1}<|z|<\infty$

$$
H(z)=\sum_{n=N_{1}}^{\infty} h[n] z^{-n}
$$

The following conditions are equivalent

1. $N_{1} \geq 0$
2. $H\left(z^{-1}\right)=\sum_{n=N_{1}}^{\infty} h[n] z^{n}$ is a convergent power series on $|z|<\frac{1}{R^{1}}$
3. 0 is a removable singularity of $H\left(z^{-1}\right)$
4. $\infty$ is removable singularity of $H(z)$
5. $\lim _{z \rightarrow 0} H\left(z^{-1}\right)$ exists and is finite
6. $\lim _{z \rightarrow \infty} H(z)$ exists and is finite ${ }^{1}$
[^0]
## 因果性

An LTI system with system function $H(z)$ is causal iff

1. the ROC is the exterior of a circle
2. $\lim _{z \rightarrow \infty} H(z)$ exists and is finite

$$
\text { causal } \Longleftrightarrow \mathbf{R O C} \text { is the exterior of a circle including } \infty
$$

An LTI system with rational system function $H(z)=\frac{N(z)}{D(z)}$ is causal iff

1. the ROC is $|z|>|p|$, where $p$ is the outermost pole
2. $\operatorname{deg} D \geq \operatorname{deg} N$

例. $H(z)=\frac{z^{3}-2 z^{2}-z}{z^{2}+\frac{1}{4} z+\frac{1}{8}}$ cannot be the system function of a causal system.

## 稳定性

Recall an LTI system is stable iff its impulse response $h \in \ell_{1}$, i.e.

$$
\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty}|h[n]|<\infty
$$

i.e. $H(z)$ converges absolutely on the unit circle $|z|=1$, so its ROC $R_{1}<|z|<R_{2}$ must satisfy $R_{1}<1<R_{2}$.
stable $\Longleftrightarrow \mathbf{R O C}$ includes the unit circle $|z|=1$

A causal LTI system with rational system function $H(z)$ is stable iff all its poles are inside the unit circle.

例. A causal system with $H(z)=\frac{1}{1-a z^{-1}}$ is stable iff $|a|<1$
例. A system with $H(z)=\frac{1}{1-a z^{-1}}$ where $|a|>1$ and ROC $|z|<|a|$ is also stable, but it is noncausal.

例

$$
H(z)=\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{z}{z-\frac{3}{2}}-\frac{z}{z+\frac{1}{2}}\right]
$$

There are two poles $p_{1}=-\frac{1}{2}$ and $p_{2}=\frac{3}{2}$.

1. $|z|>\frac{3}{2}$, causal, unstable

$$
h_{1}[n]=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^{n} u[n]-\frac{1}{2}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)^{n} u[n]
$$

![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/5693e73c-f7d3-489e-959e-fbd2437c470f-07.jpg?height=412&width=432&top_left_y=88&top_left_x=807)
2. $\frac{1}{2}<|z|<\frac{3}{2}$, noncausal, stable

$$
h_{2}[n]=-\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^{n} u[-n-1]-\frac{1}{2}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)^{n} u[n]
$$

3. $|z|<\frac{1}{2}$, noncausal, unstable

$$
h_{3}[n]=-\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^{n} u[-n-1]+\frac{1}{2}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)^{n} u[-n-1]
$$

## 线性常系数差分方程

LTI system with input and output related by

$$
\sum_{k=0}^{N} a_{k} y[n-k]=\sum_{k=0}^{M} b_{k} x[n-k]
$$

Take $z$-transform of both sides

$$
\sum_{k=0}^{N} a_{k} z^{-k} Y(z)=\sum_{k=0}^{M} b_{k} z^{-k} X(z)
$$

so

$$
H(z)=\frac{Y(z)}{X(z)}=\frac{\sum_{k=0}^{M} b_{k} z^{-k}}{\sum_{k=0}^{N} a_{k} z^{-k}}
$$

System function is always rational
差分方程 does not specify ROC! Need additional conditions (e.g. stability, causality) to determine $h[n]$.

## 例

Consider LTI system with input and output related by

$$
y[n]-\frac{1}{2} y[n-1]=x[n]+\frac{1}{3} x[n-1]
$$

System function

$$
H(z)=\frac{1+\frac{1}{3} z^{-1}}{1-\frac{1}{2} z^{-1}}
$$

Two possibilities for ROC: $|z|>\frac{1}{2}$ and $|z|<\frac{1}{2}$.

1. If $|z|>\frac{1}{2}$

$$
\frac{1}{1-\frac{1}{2} z^{-1}}=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{n} z^{-n} \stackrel{z^{-1}}{\longleftrightarrow}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{n} u[n]
$$

By linearity and time-shifting property,

$$
h[n]=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{n} u[n]+\frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{n-1} u[n-1]
$$

## 例 (cont'd)

Consider LTI system with input and output related by

$$
y[n]-\frac{1}{2} y[n-1]=x[n]+\frac{1}{3} x[n-1]
$$

System function

$$
H(z)=\frac{1+\frac{1}{3} z^{-1}}{1-\frac{1}{2} z^{-1}}
$$

Two possibilities for ROC: $|z|>\frac{1}{2}$ and $|z|<\frac{1}{2}$.
2. If $|z|<\frac{1}{2}$

$$
\frac{1}{1-\frac{1}{2} z^{-1}}=\frac{-2 z}{1-2 z}=-\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} 2^{n} z^{n} \stackrel{z^{-1}}{\longleftrightarrow}-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{n} u[-n-1]
$$

By linearity and time-shifting property,

$$
h[n]=-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{n} u[-n-1]-\frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{n-1} u[-n]
$$

## 例 (cont'd)

Consider LTI system with input and output related by

$$
y[n]-\frac{1}{2} y[n-1]=x[n]+\frac{1}{3} x[n-1]
$$

If we use Fourier transform, then frequency response is

$$
H\left(e^{j \omega}\right)=\frac{1+\frac{1}{3} e^{-j \omega}}{1-\frac{1}{2} e^{-j \omega}}
$$

and

$$
h[n]=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{n} u[n]+\frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{n-1} u[n-1]
$$

Why only one possibility?

- Fourier transform method assumes stability, requiring that ROC of $H(z)$ contain the unit circle, i.e. $|z|>\frac{1}{2}$
- In general, not applicable to unstable systems


## 例

Consider LTI system with input and output related by

$$
y[n]-\frac{3}{4} y[n-1]+\frac{1}{8} y[n-2]=2 x[n]
$$

System function

$$
H(z)=\frac{2}{1-\frac{3}{4} z^{-1}+\frac{1}{8} z^{-2}}
$$

By partial fraction expansion

$$
H(z)=\frac{2}{\left(1-\frac{1}{2} z^{-1}\right)\left(1-\frac{1}{4} z^{-1}\right)}=\frac{4}{1-\frac{1}{2} z^{-1}}-\frac{2}{1-\frac{1}{4} z^{-1}}
$$

Take inverse $z$-transform to obtain impulse response

$$
\begin{cases}h_{1}[n]=4\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{n} u[n]-2\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^{n} u[n], & \text { ROC: }|z|>\frac{1}{2} \\ h_{2}[n]=-4\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{n} u[-n-1]-2\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^{n} u[n], & \text { ROC: } \frac{1}{4}<|z|<\frac{1}{2} \\ h_{3}[n]=-4\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{n} u[-n-1]+2\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^{n} u[-n-1], & \text { ROC: }|z|<\frac{1}{4}\end{cases}
$$

## 例 (cont'd)

Find response to $x[n]=\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^{n} u[n]$.

$$
X(z)=\frac{1}{1-\frac{1}{4} z^{-1}}, \quad|z|>\frac{1}{4}
$$

$z$-transform of response

$$
Y(z)=H(z) X(z)=\frac{2}{\left(1-\frac{1}{2} z^{-1}\right)\left(1-\frac{1}{4} z^{-1}\right)} \cdot \frac{1}{1-\frac{1}{4} z^{-1}},
$$

NB. Output well-defined only for $|z|>\frac{1}{2}$ and $\frac{1}{4}<|z|<\frac{1}{2}$ !
Exercise. Verify that $h_{3} * x$ is not well-defined.
By partial fraction expansion (see slides 20-22 of Lecture 19)

$$
Y(z)=-\frac{4}{1-\frac{1}{4} z^{-1}}-\frac{2}{\left(1-\frac{1}{4} z^{-1}\right)^{2}}+\frac{8}{1-\frac{1}{2} z^{-1}}
$$

Take inverse $z$-transform to obtain response for first two cases.

Inverse $Z$-transform of $\frac{1}{\left(1-a z^{-1}\right)^{n}}$
Recall

$$
\frac{1}{1-a \zeta}=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a^{n} \zeta^{n}, \quad|a \zeta|<1
$$

and

$$
\frac{1}{1-a \zeta}=-\sum_{n=-\infty}^{-1} a^{n} \zeta^{n}, \quad|a \zeta|>1
$$

Repeat the derivation on slide 23 of Lecture 19, and let $\zeta=z^{-1}$,

$$
\binom{n+m-1}{m-1} a^{n} u[n] \stackrel{z}{\longleftrightarrow} \frac{1}{\left(1-a z^{-1}\right)^{m}}, \quad|z|>|a|
$$

and

$$
(-1)^{m}\binom{-n-1}{m-1} a^{n} u[-n-m] \stackrel{z}{\longleftrightarrow} \frac{1}{\left(1-a z^{-1}\right)^{m}}, \quad|z|<|a|
$$

## 例

Causal LTI system described by

$$
y[n]-\frac{1}{2} y[n-1]=x[n]+\frac{2}{3} x[n-1]
$$

Find response to $x[n]=\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)^{n} u[n]$
![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/5693e73c-f7d3-489e-959e-fbd2437c470f-15.jpg?height=339&width=314&top_left_y=48&top_left_x=918)

$$
\begin{gathered}
H(z)=\frac{1+\frac{2}{3} z^{-1}}{1-\frac{1}{2} z^{-1}}, \quad|z|>\frac{1}{2} \\
X(z)=\frac{1}{1+\frac{2}{3} z^{-1}}, \quad|z|>\frac{2}{3} \\
Y(z)=\frac{1}{1-\frac{1}{2} z^{-1}}, \quad|z|>\frac{1}{2} \Longrightarrow y[n]=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{n} u[n]
\end{gathered}
$$

![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/5693e73c-f7d3-489e-959e-fbd2437c470f-15.jpg?height=243&width=314&top_left_y=392&top_left_x=918)

ROC of $Y$ is larger than intersection of ROCs of $X$ and $H$ due to pole-zero cancellation at $z=-\frac{2}{3}$.
![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/5693e73c-f7d3-489e-959e-fbd2437c470f-15.jpg?height=297&width=316&top_left_y=638&top_left_x=918)

## 例

Suppose an LTI system satisfies the following,

1. output for input $x_{1}[n]=\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)^{n} u[n]$ is $y_{1}[n]=\left[a\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{n}+10\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{n}\right] u[n]$
2. output for input $x_{2}[n]=(-1)^{n}$ is $y_{2}[n]=\frac{7}{4}(-1)^{n}$

Want to find $H(z)$.

$$
\begin{gathered}
X_{1}(z)=\frac{1}{1-\frac{1}{6} z^{-1}}, \quad|z|>\frac{1}{6} \\
Y_{1}(z)=\frac{a}{1-\frac{1}{2} z^{-1}}+\frac{10}{1-\frac{1}{3} z^{-1}}, \quad|z|>\frac{1}{2}
\end{gathered}
$$

System function

$$
H(z)=\frac{Y_{1}(z)}{X_{1}(z)}=\frac{\left[(a+10)-\left(5+\frac{a}{3}\right) z^{-1}\right]\left[1-\frac{1}{6} z^{-1}\right]}{\left(1-\frac{1}{2} z^{-1}\right)\left(1-\frac{1}{3} z^{-1}\right)},
$$

By 2, $H(-1)=\frac{7}{4} \Longrightarrow a=-9 \Longrightarrow H(z)=\frac{\left(1-2 z^{-1}\right)\left(1-\frac{1}{6} z^{-1}\right)}{\left(1-\frac{1}{2} z^{-1}\right)\left(1-\frac{1}{3} z^{-1}\right)}$

## 例 (cont'd)

Three possibilities for ROC of $H(z)=\frac{\left(1-2 z^{-1}\right)\left(1-\frac{1}{6} z^{-1}\right)}{\left(1-\frac{1}{2} z^{-1}\right)\left(1-\frac{1}{3} z^{-1}\right)}$

- $|z|<\frac{1}{3}$
- $\frac{1}{3}<|z|<\frac{1}{2}$
- $|z|>\frac{1}{2}$

By the convolution property, ROC of $Y_{1}$ contains the intersection of the ROCs of $X_{1}$ and $H \Longrightarrow$ ROC of $H$ is $|z|>\frac{1}{2} \Longrightarrow$ stable.
Also $H(\infty)=1$ is finite ⟹ causal

$$
H(z)=\frac{1-\frac{13}{6} z^{-1}+\frac{1}{3} z^{-2}}{1-\frac{5}{6} z^{-1}+\frac{1}{6} z^{-2}}
$$

差分方程

$$
y[n]-\frac{5}{6} y[n-1]+\frac{1}{6} y[n-2]=x[n]-\frac{13}{6} x[n-1]+\frac{1}{3} x[n-2]
$$

LTI systems in 串联系统

$$
Y=\left(X H_{1}\right) H_{2}=X\left(H_{1} H_{2}\right)=\left(X H_{2}\right) H_{1}
$$

## 系统互连

LTI systems in systems in 反馈系统

$$
\begin{gathered}
y=h_{1} *\left(x-h_{2} * y\right) \\
h=?
\end{gathered}
$$

![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/5693e73c-f7d3-489e-959e-fbd2437c470f-21.jpg?height=323&width=769&top_left_y=208&top_left_x=452)
$Y=H_{1} X-H_{1} H_{2} Y$
$H=\frac{Y}{X}=\frac{H_{1}}{1+H_{1} H_{2}}$

## 单边 Z 变换

The (bilateral) $z$-transform of a DT signal $x$

$$
X(z)=\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty} x[n] z^{-n}
$$

The unilateral $z$-transform of $x$ is

$$
X(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} x[n] x^{-n}
$$

also denoted

$$
X=\mathcal{U} z\{x\}, \quad x[n] \stackrel{u z}{\longleftrightarrow} X(z)
$$

Note $\mathcal{U} \mathcal{Z}\{x\}=\mathcal{Z}\{x u\}$, where $u$ is the unit step function.

- ROC of $X$ is always the exterior of a circle, including $\infty$

For rational $X(z)=\frac{N(z)}{D(z)}$, we always have $\operatorname{deg} N \leq \operatorname{deg} D$

- $\mathcal{Z}\{x\}=\mathcal{U Z}\{x\}$ iff $x[n]=0$ for $n<0$


## 例s

The calculation of unilateral $z$-transforms is almost the same as for bilateral $z$-transforms. Remember to sum over only $n \geq 0$.

例. $x_{1}[n]=a^{n} u[n]$,

$$
X_{1}(z)=X_{1}(z)=\frac{1}{1-a z^{-1}}, \quad|z|>|a|
$$

例. $x_{2}[n]=a^{n+1} u[n+1]=x_{1}[n+1]$,

$$
X_{2}(z)=z X_{1}(z)=\frac{z}{1-a z^{-1}}, \quad|z|>|a|
$$

But

$$
X_{2}(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} x[n] z^{-n}=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a^{n+1} z^{-n}=\frac{a}{1-a z^{-1}},|z|>|a|
$$

## 例s

The calculation of inverse unilateral $z$-transforms is the same as for bilateral $z$-transforms, but we can only recover $x[n]$ for $n \geq 0!$
例. Given unilateral $z$-transform

$$
X(z)=\frac{3-\frac{5}{6} z^{-1}}{\left(1-\frac{1}{4} z^{-1}\right)\left(1-\frac{1}{3} z^{-1}\right)}=\frac{1}{1-\frac{1}{4} z^{-1}}+\frac{2}{1-\frac{1}{3} z^{-1}}
$$

the only possibility for ROC is $|z| \geq \frac{1}{3}$. Thus

$$
x[n]=\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^{n}+2\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{n}, \quad n \geq 0
$$

X provides no information about $x[n]$ for $n<0$
例. $\frac{z^{2}}{z-a}$ is not a valid unilateral $z$-transform, since $\operatorname{deg} D=1<2=\operatorname{deg} N$

Properties of 单边 Z 变换
Many properties are the same as for bilateral $z$-transform

| Property | Signal | Unilateral $z$-transform |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| - | $x[n]$ | $X(z)$ |
| - | $y[n]$ | $y(z)$ |
| Linearity | $a x[n]+b y[n]$ | $a \mathfrak{X}(z)+b y(z)$ |
| Scaling in $z$ domain | $z_{0}^{n} x[n]$ | $\mathcal{X}\left(z / z_{0}\right)$ |
| Time expansion | $x_{(k)}[n]$ | $X\left(z^{k}\right)$ |
| Conjugation | $x^{*}[n]$ | $X^{*}\left(z^{*}\right)$ |
| Differentiation in $z$ domain | $n x[n]$ | $-z \frac{d}{d z} \mathcal{X}(z)$ |
| 初值定理 | $x[0]=\lim _{z \rightarrow \infty} \mathfrak{X}(z)$ |  |

## Properties of Unilateral $z$-transform

Convolution Property. If $x[n]=y[n]=0$ for $n<0$, then

$$
(x * y)[n] \stackrel{u z}{\longleftrightarrow} X(z) y(z)
$$

Proof. Note $(x * y)[n]=0$ for $n<0$ and $\mathcal{U} Z\{x\}=Z\{x\}$ if $x=x u$.

$$
\mathcal{U} z\{x * y\}=\mathcal{Z}\{x * y\}=\mathcal{Z}\{x\} z\{y\}=\mathcal{U} z\{x\} \mathcal{U} z\{y\}
$$

Caution. The assumption $x[n]=y[n]=0$ for $n<0$ is important!
例. $x[n]=\delta[n]-\delta[n-1], y[n]=\delta[n+1]$,

$$
X(z)=1-z^{-1}, \quad y(z)=0
$$

Note $(x * y)[n]=\delta[n+1]-\delta[n]$, and

$$
\mathcal{U} z\{x * y\}=-1 \neq \mathfrak{X}(z) y(z)
$$

## Properties of Unilateral $z$-transform

Time delay.

$$
x[n-m] \stackrel{u z}{\longleftrightarrow} x^{-m}\left(\mathfrak{X}(z)+\sum_{k=1}^{m} x[-k] z^{k}\right)
$$

Proof.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal{U} z\{x[n-m]\} & =\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} x[n-m] z^{-n} \\
& =z^{-m} \sum_{k=-m}^{\infty} x[k] z^{-k} \\
& =z^{-m}\left(X(z)+\sum_{k=-m}^{-1} x[k] z^{-k}\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

## Properties of Unilateral $z$-transform

Time advance.

$$
x[n+m] \stackrel{u z}{\longleftrightarrow} z^{m}\left(\mathcal{X}(z)-\sum_{k=0}^{m-1} x[k] z^{-k}\right)
$$

Proof.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal{U} z\{x[n+m]\} & =\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} x[n+m] z^{-n} \\
& =z^{m} \sum_{k=m}^{\infty} x[k] z^{-k} \\
& =z^{m}\left(\mathcal{X}(z)-\sum_{k=0}^{m-1} x[k] z^{-k}\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

## 线性常系数差分方程

Consider difference equation

$$
\sum_{k=0}^{N} a_{k} y[n-k]=\sum_{k=0}^{M} b_{k} x[n-k]
$$

with initial condition $y[-1], y[-2], \ldots, y[-N]$ and causal input, i.e. $x[n]=0$ for $n<0$.
Take unilateral $z$-transform of both sides

$$
\sum_{k=0}^{N} a_{k} z^{-k}\left[y(z)+\sum_{\ell=-k}^{-1} y[\ell] z^{-\ell}\right]=\sum_{k=0}^{M} b_{k} z^{-k} \mathfrak{X}(z)
$$

so

$$
y(z)=\underbrace{\frac{\sum_{k=0}^{M} b_{k} z^{-k}}{\sum_{k=0}^{N} a_{k} z^{-k}} \mathcal{X}(z)}_{\text {零状态响应 }} \underbrace{-\frac{\sum_{k=0}^{N} a_{k} z^{-k} \sum_{\ell=-k}^{-1} y[\ell] z^{-\ell}}{\sum_{k=0}^{N} a_{k} z^{-k}}}_{\text {零输入响应 }}
$$

## 例

Consider difference equation

$$
y[n]+2 y[n-1]=x[n]
$$

with initial condition $y[-1]=\beta$ and $x[n]=\alpha u[n]$.
Take unilateral $z$-transform of both sides

$$
y(z)+2 z^{-1}(y(z)+y[-1] z)=x(z)=\frac{\alpha}{1-z^{-1}}
$$

so

$$
y(z)=\underbrace{\frac{1}{1+2 z^{-1}} \cdot \frac{\alpha}{1-z^{-1}}}_{\text {零状态响应 }}+\underbrace{\frac{-2 \beta}{1+2 z^{-1}}}_{\text {零输入响应 }}
$$

例 (cont'd)

$$
y(z)=\underbrace{\frac{1}{1+2 z^{-1}} \cdot \frac{\alpha}{1-z^{-1}}}_{\text {零状态响应 }}+\underbrace{\frac{-2 \beta}{1+2 z^{-1}}}_{\text {零输入响应 }}
$$

Zero-input response. $\alpha=0$

$$
y_{z i}[n]=-2 \beta(-2)^{n}, \quad n \geq 0
$$

Zero-state response. $\beta=0$, system at initial rest

$$
\begin{gathered}
y_{z s}(z)=\frac{1}{1+2 z^{-1}} \cdot \frac{\alpha}{1-z^{-1}}=\frac{2 \alpha / 3}{1+2 z^{-1}}+\frac{\alpha / 3}{1-z^{-1}} \\
y_{z s}[n]=\frac{2 \alpha}{3}(-2)^{n}+\frac{\alpha}{3}, \quad n \geq 0
\end{gathered}
$$

## 例

## Consider difference equation

$$
y[n]-y[n-1]-2 y[n-2]=x[n]+2 x[n-2]
$$

with initial condition $y[-1]=2, y[-2]=-\frac{1}{2}$ and $x[n]=u[n]$.

## Take unilateral $z$-transform of both sides

$$
y(z)-z^{-1}(y(z)+y[-1] z)-2 z^{-2}\left(y(z)+y[-1] z+y[-2] z^{2}\right)=\left(1+2 z^{-2}\right) \mathfrak{X}(z)
$$

so

$$
\begin{aligned}
y(z) & =\underbrace{\frac{1+2 z^{-2}}{1-z^{-1}-2 z^{-2}} \cdot \frac{1}{1-z^{-1}}}_{\text {零状态响应 }}+\underbrace{\frac{2 z^{-1} y[-1]+y[-1]+2 y[-2]}{1-z^{-1}-2 z^{-2}}}_{\text {零输入响应 }} \\
& =\underbrace{\frac{1+2 z^{-2}}{\left(1+z^{-1}\right)\left(1-2 z^{-1}\right)\left(1-z^{-1}\right)}}_{\text {零状态响应 }}+\underbrace{\frac{4 z^{-1}+1}{\left(1+z^{-1}\right)\left(1-2 z^{-1}\right)}}_{\text {零输入响应 }}
\end{aligned}
$$

## 例 (cont'd)

For the 零输入响应,

$$
y_{z i}(z)=\frac{4 z^{-1}+1}{\left(1+z^{-1}\right)\left(1-2 z^{-1}\right)}=\frac{-1}{1+z^{-1}}+\frac{2}{1-2 z^{-1}}
$$

SO

$$
y_{z i}[n]=2^{n+1}+(-1)^{n+1}, \quad n \geq 0
$$

For the 零状态响应,

$$
\begin{aligned}
y_{z s}(z) & =\frac{1+2 z^{-2}}{\left(1+z^{-1}\right)\left(1-2 z^{-1}\right)\left(1-z^{-1}\right)} \\
& =\frac{1 / 2}{1+z^{-1}}+\frac{2}{1-2 z^{-1}}+\frac{-3 / 2}{1-z^{-1}}
\end{aligned}
$$

So

$$
y_{z s}[n]=\frac{1}{2}(-1)^{n}+2^{n+1}-\frac{3}{2}, \quad n \geq 0
$$
